notes: Tickets for the two New York concerts go on sale at the box office and are gone by the next day. About 2,900 people will see each show.

The Beatles land at Kennedy Airport at 1:20 p.m. Eastern. About 3,000 fans are there. A press conference follows, and the band is taken to the Plaza Hotel. "I Want to Hold Your Hand" is the No. 1 single in America.

Live from Studio 50 at 8:00 p.m. Eastern. Five songs, 728 seats in the theater, and about 73 million people watching. They had taped a second Sullivan appearance earlier the same day, for broadcast on February 23.

They reach Washington by train through a snowstorm and play the Washington Coliseum. The stage is a boxing ring in the round, so they turn the gear a quarter turn between songs. The listed start is 8:00 p.m.

location: Back in New York. A crowd meets the train at Penn Station. The first of two 34-minute sets begins at 7:45 p.m. Backstage, Swan Records hands them a gold disc for "She Loves You."
The second set begins at 11:15 p.m. The hall later asks the promoter not to bring them back.
A third appearance, broadcast from the Deauville Hotel in Miami Beach at 8:00 p.m. Eastern.

notes: The first American visit ends. The Beatles fly back to England.
